series: The Dark Side of Once Upon a Time
title: Rumpelstiltskin: The Name That Broke the Bargain
version_scope: Brothers Grimm, final 1857 German edition, as rendered in Margaret Hunt's 1884 English translation. This is one documented literary version, not a claim about the tale's first or only form.

sources.edition: Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, 7th edition (1857), vol. 1, tale 55, Rumpelstilzchen; translated by Margaret Hunt as Grimm's Household Tales, vol. 1 (London: George Bell and Sons, 1884), tale 55, Rumpelstiltskin, pp. 221–225.
sources.scope_note: The linked online transcription is Hunt's English text based on the Grimm tale; the episode identifies the German source edition and translation separately. The 1857 story ends with Rumpelstiltskin stamping his foot into the floor and wrenching it free.

narration: A miller boasts that his daughter can spin straw into gold. The king locks her in a straw-filled room: “Gold by morning—or die.” A tiny stranger appears. He spins the straw in exchange for her necklace. The next night, the king brings more straw. The stranger takes her ring in exchange for gold. On the third night, she has nothing left to pay. The king promises to make her queen. The stranger demands her first child. She agrees. The gold earns her the crown. When her baby is born, the stranger returns to claim it. She begs for time. He gives her three days to guess his name. A messenger finds him dancing in the forest and overhears his secret. The queen cries, “Rumpelstiltskin!” The little man vanishes in fury. Her child is safe.
